from.place: The open projection map used to interpret the open scalar comparison; this node isolates existing intrinsic open-adjunction definitions from the integral coefficient setting.

title: Intrinsic open projection inverse is invertible
statement: For any coefficient family [def-sp-open-coefficient-adjunction-data], open immersion j:U→X [def-weil-open-immersion], tensor models a on U and b on X, and arbitrary unbounded derived module objects M on U and N on X [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the canonical open projection inverse openProjectionInverse R j a b M N is an isomorphism. Its open adjunct is exactly unit tensor identity followed by the inverse canonical restriction tensorator. No finiteness, boundedness, quasi-compactness, coefficient flatness, or integral completion is assumed.

proof.text: Identify the actual open extension with a coefficient equivalence followed by localizedModuleExtension. Construct the equivalence from proEtale_ringed_open_comparison and the scalar equivalence for the given coefficient isomorphism; uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the resulting extension. Derive this presentation termwise and through localization. The localized unit is invertible by subterminality of the open object, so the actual derived open extension is fully faithful.

Represent the slice object by an arbitrary complex and resolve the ambient tensor factor by a flat-term K-flat complex. proEtaleMixedTensor_existsUnique computes tensor against this representative. The existing extension_total_iso moves exact slice extension through that signed total tensor, so tensoring an extended object remains in the essential image of extension. Transport this image assertion through the derived slice-presentation isomorphism.

The counit on the target tensor is invertible because that tensor lies in the essential image of the fully faithful extension. The specified adjunct of openProjectionInverse is the tensor of the invertible unit and identity followed by the inverse canonical tensor comparison; hence it is invertible. The hom-equivalence formula expresses its transpose as extension of the adjunct followed by the invertible counit, proving the original specified map invertible.

theorem openProjectionInverse_isIso (R : Coefficients.{u}) {U V : Scheme.{u}}
    (j : U ⟶ V) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (a : ProEtaleTensorModel U (R.ring U)) (b : ProEtaleTensorModel V (R.ring V))
    (M : DerivedCategory (pbcModules U (R.ring U)))
    (N : DerivedCategory (pbcModules V (R.ring V))) :
    IsIso (openProjectionInverse R j a b M N)
